ios.desc:
ScrollGuard helps you cut down on mindless screen time so you can use social media to stay connected, without getting sucked into the endless feed.

Instead of blocking entire sites or apps, ScrollGuard uses a Safari browser extension to hide the most addictive parts of social media websites: endless feeds, Reels, Stories, Explore pages and other attention traps. Because it filters content directly in the browser, you don’t have to lock yourself out of your accounts, rely on willpower, or delete anything. You keep the useful parts, without the constant pull to keep scrolling.

You choose what to hide, so you can still get value from social media without getting trapped in the scroll.

Features:

    Hide Reels, Stories, Explore and other addictive sections of popular social platforms
    Toggle each element on or off with simple switches

Premium Features:
    Set unlimited custom filters

Terms of Use: https://scrollguard.app/terms

android.desc:
ScrollGuard – Block Reels, Shorts & Stop Scrolling 🚫
ScrollGuard is a productivity app designed to help you stop wasting time on addictive short-form videos and endless feeds. Whether it’s Reels, Shorts, or doom-scrolling, ScrollGuard helps you regain your focus, reduce screen time, and improve your digital wellbeing so you can spend more time on what truly matters.

Why ScrollGuard? 🤔
Short-form videos, Reels, Shorts, and infinite feeds are designed to keep you hooked, leading to increased screen time, distractions, and lost productivity. Most app blockers cut you off from entire apps, making it hard to stay connected while avoiding the real problem: doom-scrolling. ScrollGuard takes a smarter approach: it lets you reduce screen time and use social media in a mindful, balanced way by disabling only the addictive content, not the entire app.

Key Features 🌟
- Disable Reels & Shorts Without Blocking the App: Instantly block Shorts and Reels on popular platforms, while keeping messaging and other core features available.
- Anti-Scroll Mode: If you scroll for too long, a customizable popup prompts you to pause for a minute or quit instantly. All settings are fully customizable per app.
- Strict Mode with Accountability: Protect your settings with a password. Share the password with an accountability partner to help you stay committed to your time management goals.
- Custom Break Messages: Personalize the popup with your own motivational reminders for extra encouragement.
- Pause, With Limits: Easily pause protection for planned exceptions, with safeguards to prevent endless pausing.
- Usage Statistics: You can only improve what you can measure. Track your daily screen time within ScrollGuard to help you reduce screen time and set better goals.
How ScrollGuard Improves Digital Wellbeing 📉
- Stop Doom-Scrolling: Block addictive content like Reels, Shorts, and infinite feeds so you spend less time trapped in mindless scrolling.
- Reduce Screen Time: Effectively cut down on unnecessary screen time by eliminating the most distracting social media features.
- Build Self-Control: The anti-scroll popup interrupts unconscious habits, giving you space to choose whether to keep scrolling or take a healthy break.
- Boost Productivity: With fewer distractions, save hours every day for study, work, hobbies, or family.
- Support Accountability: Lock settings to involve a friend or partner, making it easier to stay on track and achieve your digital wellbein

quotes.text:
Last year I built an Android app to block Reels and Shorts while keeping "healthy" features like stories and DMs. I didn't want to block the whole app. I just wanted to message friends and see their posts without losing an hour scrolling on Reels. This was the HN post for the Android version: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44923520

When people asked for an iOS version, I thought it was not possible. Apple is way more restrictive and doesn't allow that level of app access.

But I ended up building the iOS app using a different approach. On iOS, it uses WebApps. It's not exactly the same experience as the native app, but it works surprisingly well.

I also combined it with iOS Shortcuts to auto-redirect the native apps to WebApps, so I can keep Instagram installed for notifications but get sent to the WebApp without Reels and any feed when I tap.

Curious what you think, especially about the WebApp approach on iOS.
